title: Number of Distinct Substrings in a String
summary: For a string s, calculate the count of unique substrings that can be formed by removing any combination of characters from the start and end of s.
statement: For a string s, calculate the count of unique substrings that can be formed by removing any combination of characters from the start and end of s.
constraints: 1 <= len(s) <= 500; s contains lowercase English letters.
A substring is a nonempty contiguous slice obtained by trimming a prefix and suffix.
Return the number of different substring values, counting duplicate occurrences once.
reference_solution:
def count_distinct_substrings(s):
    return len({s[i:j] for i in range(len(s)) for j in range(i+1,len(s)+1)})
hints: Distinctness concerns substring values, not positions.
Insert every nonempty contiguous slice into a set.
Loop start i and exclusive end j>i; return the set size.
Every substring has one such pair of endpoints, and set membership removes repeated occurrences.
editorial: Every substring has one such pair of endpoints, and set membership removes repeated occurrences.

tests.explanation: Enumerating contiguous slices and deduplicating them leaves 21 values.
The only distinct substrings are a, aa, and aaa.
